beats.text: Thirteen light-years from here, a star is orbiting the galaxy the wrong way.
beats.anchor: its light left it about 13 years ago

beats.text: Almost every star near us, the Sun included, circles the Milky Way in the same direction.
This one goes backwards, so it passes us at about two hundred and ninety kilometres every second.
beats.header: ≈ 293 km/s · Earth to Moon in 22 minutes
beats.anchor: Earth to the Moon in 22 minutes

beats.text: For a star, it races across our sky: it moves the width of a full Moon in about two centuries.
beats.header: 8.6″ a year · 2nd-fastest star in our sky

beats.text: Its low metal content says it is ancient, and one theory says it was born in a smaller galaxy the Milky Way swallowed.
beats.header: Pictured: Omega Centauri, suspected core · debated

beats.text: So the next time the night sky looks perfectly still, remember
beats.header: Kapteyn's Star: still going the wrong way
